version.changelog: Clearer disclosure of what is stored and where

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed local developer-assistant memory workflow, but users should understand that it automatically stores durable work notes, contacts, and project records on the machine.

dimensions.detail: Reading and writing code, tests, config, and local developer notes is proportionate to a day-to-day developer skill; the artifacts repeatedly instruct redaction of credentials and customer data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected package is markdown/json only; no executable scripts, install hooks, or remote payload loaders were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions scope reads and writes to declared Clawic data paths and user-pointed repositories, with explicit limits to ignore indexed paths outside ~/Clawic/data/ and not transmit data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill intentionally uses persistent local memory and shared contacts/projects files without per-write permission, but this behavior is disclosed, locally confined, and tied to the skill purpose.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The package is coherent with its stated developer purpose: it gives guidance for coding, bugs, tests, reviews, dependencies, migrations, shipping, incidents, and security checks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want this skill to maintain local, cross-session developer memory under ~/Clawic/data/, including repo notes, estimates, releases, incidents, project status, and limited work contacts. Review or clear those files periodically if you do not want that context retained or shared with other Clawic skills.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The credential strings appear in instructions saying not to store secrets and to save only pointers such as env/keychain/file locators; I found no instruction to read or exfiltrate private key contents.
[EA1] expected: The 'run arbitrary code' phrase is a supply-chain warning about package install scripts, not an instruction granting unrestricted tool access.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic local memory writes and deletions are real and disclosed; they are bounded to configPaths and announced, so this is user-awareness guidance rather than a malicious or hidden behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: The shared-contact retirement deletion is limited to contacts this work involves and, by SKILL.md, only rows this skill wrote itself; users should still be aware shared local records may be changed.
[EA2] expected: The migration guidance emphasizes checking rollback paths and, elsewhere, destructive statements are governed by risk_confirm with explicit confirmation when true.
[SQP-3] expected: The changelog language instruction is ordinary localization to the user's language and does not create a security issue in context.
[other] expected: The SARIF concern about persistent profiling is partly valid as a privacy note, but the storage is disclosed, local, scoped to developer work, and explicitly excludes secrets and customer data.
